differences.title: 1. DATA TYPES
differences.leftDesc: Supports advanced types like JSONB, arrays, hstore, and custom types for complex data.
differences.rightDesc: Primarily uses standard SQL data types, well-understood and widely compatible.

differences.title: 2. EXTENSIBILITY
differences.leftDesc: Allows custom functions, operators, data types, and procedural languages.
differences.rightDesc: Supports stored procedures, triggers, and user-defined functions.

differences.title: 3. CONCURRENCY CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: Uses Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) for better read/write performance.
differences.rightDesc: Relies more on table and row locking, can lead to contention.

differences.title: 4. ACID COMPLIANCE
differences.leftDesc: Ensures Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability for transactions.
differences.rightDesc: Generally ACID compliant, with some nuances depending on storage engine.

differences.title: 5. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Often excels with complex queries, large datasets, and analytical workloads.
differences.rightDesc: Typically performs very well for read-heavy applications and simpler queries.

differences.title: 6. REPLICATION
differences.leftDesc: Offers logical and physical replication, streaming replication, and synchronous/asynchronous options.
differences.rightDesc: Provides master-master and master-slave replication, often well-supported.

differences.title: 7. JSON SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Advanced JSONB type with indexing and querying capabilities for JSON data.
differences.rightDesc: Supports JSON data type with basic validation and string manipulation.
